sections.h2: Who bills and collects Pike County property tax?
sections.html:
Land, house, vehicle and boat taxes in Pike County are billed and collected by the Collector of Revenue, whose office is at 115 West Main, Bowling Green, MO 63334. Call 573-324-3281. Weekday hours run 8 to 4:30, and the office closes from noon to 1 for lunch outside tax season.

More than $20 million moves through the office yearly, and each month it is sent on to schools, roads, cities, fire districts, levees and drainage districts. The collector works from the assessor's records and has no power to alter a value, legal description or mailing address, so take those requests to the Pike County Assessor at 573-324-3261. The collector's general tax page has the current wording.

Pike County sits on Missouri's eastern edge along the Mississippi River, and Bowling Green is the seat. Other cities are Clarksville, Curryville, Frankford and Louisiana. An estimated 17,955 people lived here in July 2025, spread over 7,682 housing units. Owners occupy 73.3 percent of the homes in use. Median owned-home value is $146,000, rent is $778 monthly and household income is $54,989. With only 20 building permits in 2025, this is a small market dominated by owners.

With home values that modest, one delinquent year can be a large share of what a house is worth. The timing of the bill matters more here than the rate itself.

sections.h2: When bills are mailed and due
sections.html:
November 1 is the mailing date for statements. A bill that fails to arrive by mid-November deserves a call to the collector, since the tax and late charges apply either way. A December 31 postmark keeps you on time. Later postmarks come back unprocessed unless interest and penalty are enclosed.

Neither partial nor pro-rated payments are taken. On a parcel with several unpaid years, the oldest is applied first under RSMo 140.110. A single check may cover multiple bills, provided every statement goes in with it.

sections.h2: How can I pay a Pike County property tax bill?
sections.html:
Options include the courthouse window, the mail, the phone and the web. Only the window takes cash. Otherwise the office accepts checks, money orders, cashier's checks, certified checks and credit or debit cards, the cards carrying a convenience fee. Mail counts as paid on the postmark date and the receipt returns the same way.

  • E-check: a flat 80 cents.
  • Visa, Mastercard and Discover: 2.35 percent of the total, minimum $1.00.
  • American Express: 2.95 percent of the total, minimum $1.00.
  • Automatic installments: bank draft under the free Pre-Pay program, described below.

sections.h2: Assessment rates and the appeal calendar
sections.html:
Each January 1 is the assessment date. A house is counted at 19 percent of market value, farmland at 12 percent of what it produces, and all other real estate at 32 percent. Reviews come every two years, and state law wants values within 5 percent of the market.

Keep this calendar nearby if you plan to dispute a value:

Pike County assessment calendar
DateEvent
January 1Assessment date
March 1Personal property list due
June 15Notice of increased value mailed
July 1Totals go to the County Clerk
Third Monday in JulyBoard of Equalization hearings begin
September 30State-level appeal due

Staff will go over your parcel with you and show how the value was reached. Escrow customers should alert the lender the moment a notice comes, so the monthly payment can be adjusted. The assessor's site is pike.missouriassessors.com.

sections.h2: Can I dispute a bill without missing the deadline?
sections.html:
Yes, though an appeal does not move the December 31 due date. You may appeal before paying. To protest, deliver the full bill to the collector by December 31 with "paid under protest" written on the check, plus a statement of your grounds that names the fair market value you claim.

Once the county board has a dispute, wait for its decision letter; the next filing is due thirty days after the letter's date. An attorney must file for property owned by a trust, LLC, corporation or estate. The State Tax Commission guide walks through the forms.

sections.h2: Unpaid tax and the August sale
sections.html:
A parcel entering its third year of delinquent tax goes to the August sale under RSMo 140.160. Bidding starts at 10 a.m. outside the courthouse's south side, on August's fourth Monday. A local newspaper carries the listing three weeks running, with the final notice at least 15 days ahead.

  • The opening bid equals all taxes, interest and charges.
  • The winning bidder pays immediately and receives a Certificate of Purchase.
  • Possession stays with the owner through a one-year redemption period (RSMo 140.310).
  • Money paid above the opening bid goes to the County Treasurer, and the owner of record can claim it. After three years it goes to the schools (RSMo 140.230).

A very high share of owners pay after the advertisement and before the sale. The office gives no legal advice, so a seller facing a listing should speak with a Missouri attorney.

sections.h2: Programs that can lower the cost
sections.html:
Three programs deserve a call. The collector's Pre-Pay plan draws monthly amounts from a bank account at no charge, with the first installments based on the prior year's totals and the balance collected on November 15. It requires a yearly bill of at least $100 for real estate and $100 for personal property, and a voided check to enroll.

The Senior Tax Freeze for 2027 takes applications from March 15 to June 30, 2027. The applicant must hold the deed to a primary residence in Pike County, be 62 by January 1 of the application year, be a Missouri resident and have no delinquent taxes. The state also runs the Property Tax Credit claim, which gives qualifying seniors and 100 percent disabled individuals up to $1,100 as owners, based on income and tax paid (Missouri Department of Revenue).

Settle every open year before the sale, because the collector will not accept the current bill until older years are paid. The Pike office does not pro-rate a bill, so the buyer and seller split is worked out by the closing agent in the contract.

If you owe more than one year, call the collector in Bowling Green for exact payoff figures with interest. Get the legal description from the assessor, and confirm the mailing address on file, before you list, because the collector cannot fix either one. In a cash sale the payoff still comes out of your proceeds at closing, and the buyer does not need lender approval of a clean tax record first.

faqs.q: What is the Pike County property tax deadline?
faqs.a: December 31, judged by postmark. Statements are mailed on November 1, and a payment postmarked after December 31 is returned unless interest and penalty are included.

faqs.q: Can I pay half of my bill now and half later?
faqs.a: No. The collector accepts no partial payments, and payments for the wrong amount are returned. The free Pre-Pay installment plan is the way to spread the cost through the year.

faqs.q: How do I get a value corrected?
faqs.a: Call the Pike County Assessor at 573-324-3261 before the county board opens its July hearings. If that fails, the State Tax Commission appeal is due by September 30 or thirty days after the board mails its letter.

faqs.q: When is the Pike County tax sale?
faqs.a: The auction runs at 10 a.m. on the fourth Monday of August, on the south side of the courthouse. Only parcels with a third year of delinquent tax must be offered, and an owner can pay before the sale to remove the parcel.

faqs.q: Who qualifies for the Senior Tax Freeze?
faqs.a: An applicant must hold the deed to a primary Pike County residence, be 62 by January 1 of the application year, live in Missouri and owe no delinquent tax. Applications for 2027 run from March 15 to June 30, 2027.
